$comment: XY Forever serial protocol v1: the single source. scripts/protogen.py validates it and generates target/usb_proto_ids.hpp, xy_forever/usb_proto_ids.py, clients/ts/src/v1.ts and docs/PROTOCOL.md. Describes the protocol as the device speaks it today; planned additions are only in 'reserved'. `since` on a command, status, event or hello key is the version that introduced its current form. `streams` are byte streams with the frames a correct parser finds in them (direction to_device: requests, which the simulator test also sends to the device code).

protocol.name: XY Forever serial protocol
intro: XY Forever is a firmware and mod manager for the teenage engineering OP-XY. While its menu runs, the OP-XY's processor B answers this protocol over USB. Tools use it to list, read, write and delete files, take screenshots, stage and install builds, set the default firmware and restart the device.

Transport: USB CDC serial, the raw frame stream (table below). The device answers only while the XY Forever menu runs: after an XY Forever restart, or when the OP-XY is powered on with PLAY held (release it at the logo).
All numbers are little-endian. Byte counts are in decimal unless written in hex (`0x...`).

transport.doc: How a tool reaches the protocol. `verified` is true for facts read from device sessions or the code, false for facts nobody has checked yet.

usb_vendor_id.doc: teenage engineering: the stock serial identity (`scripts/usb_timeline.py`), used as fallback when a boot-time check fails

usb_product_id.doc: the stock OS uses the same id with no serial interface (MTP, vendor class 0xFF; another mode is 0x8021, class 0x01), so a filter on both ids finds only XY Forever's service on the stock identity; a tool must accept this pair and `product_usb_ids`

product_usb_ids.doc: the composite (this CDC serial interface, MTP on interface 2) uses 2367:0021 (xyf_build.py MTP_USB_IDS); its device class 0xEF (IAD) distinguishes it from stock OS MTP and the stock serial fallback. XY Forever keeps this pair for good (#58)

usb_product.doc: the product string as macOS reports it in the session logs (two log lines show `OP-XY Boot`); informational: filter on the ids

interface_classes.doc: USB CDC: communications (0x02) and data (0x0A); on macOS the port is `/dev/cu.usbmodem*`

stream.doc: the CDC data interface carries exactly the frame stream described here, in both directions, with no other framing; the simulator's TCP port carries the same bytes

line_settings.doc: baud rate, parity, stop bits and flow control do not matter (an API that needs a baud rate may pass any); open the port raw (no echo, no line editing)

control_lines.doc: whether the device needs DTR or RTS set: `uv run xyf-host` leaves them as macOS sets them on open

usb_serial_number.doc: macOS names the port `cu.usbmodem<string>1`, which suggests a serial-number string; a browser may need one to find the port again after a restart without asking the user

simulator_port.doc: default TCP port of the device simulator (`uv run -m xy_forever.sim`, 127.0.0.1 only; its control port is a separate setting, 7342 by default), one client at a time

frame.crc: zlib CRC-32 (polynomial 0xEDB88320, initial value and final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF, as Python's zlib.crc32) over every byte before it

fields.name: magic
fields.doc: ASCII `XF` (0x58 0x46)

fields.name: type
fields.doc: message type: a request (< 0x80), its reply (request type + 0x80) or an event

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: chosen by the tool for each request; the reply carries the same value; events use 0

fields.name: length
fields.doc: payload bytes, at most `max_payload`

fields.name: payload
fields.doc: `length` bytes

fields.name: crc
fields.doc: CRC-32 of magic, type, seq, length and payload

constants.name: max_payload
constants.doc: largest payload in either direction; a frame announcing more is treated as noise

constants.name: max_data
constants.doc: largest file or image data in one reply

constants.name: max_read
constants.doc: largest `length` of a ranged `file.read`, and the most data `screen.read` returns per reply

constants.name: put_chunk
constants.doc: data bytes per `stage.data` request that tools should send: the device's USB receive buffer holds 2048 bytes, and a 4 KiB frame overflowed it (no reply)

constants.name: max_path
constants.doc: largest device path, including its NUL

constants.name: idle_reset_ms
constants.doc: the device drops a partial frame once its receive buffer has been empty for this long

constants.name: max_hello
constants.doc: largest `hello` text (240 before 1.25, 224 before 1.23, 200 before 1.15); a build's text is fixed but for its run-time parts (221 bytes in the product build without stage 2, nothing asked, serial on), checked when it is compiled

rules.name: request_types
rules.text: Request types are below 0x80. A reply has the request's type plus 0x80 and the request's seq, and its payload starts with a u32 status code (0 = ok); the fields listed under each command follow it.

rules.name: one_outstanding
rules.text: One request at a time: send a request, then wait for its reply (or the command's timeout) before sending the next. The device handles requests one by one and its receive buffer is small.

rules.name: hello_first
rules.text: Send `hello` first. Until the device has answered a `hello` since it started, it answers every other request with status `state` and does nothing.

rules.name: unsupported_types
rules.text: A request type this build does not answer gets status `unsupported`. The `cmds` key of the `hello` reply lists the types a build answers; tools send no others and tell the user to update XY Forever instead. A command with an optional build switch is missing from a build without it; a command whose switch is not optional is in every build that has this service (the firmware does not build without it).

rules.name: pre_v1
rules.text: Devices that send `proto=1` and no `cmds` speak 1.0 without the `hello` keys added in 1.1: tools treat every 1.0 command as answered (one the build lacks gets status 2) and expect no status above 13.

rules.name: stale_replies
rules.text: Tools drop frames whose seq or type does not match the request they wait for, and reset their frame parser after a timeout: a late reply to an earlier request is then ignored.

rules.name: link_lost
rules.text: After a `link` error, later file commands return `link` at once while the outstanding request remains unresolved. B never resets itself to recover a lost link; a power cycle restores the processors together.

rules.name: events
rules.text: Events are frames the device sends on its own, with seq 0 and a type of 0x80 or above that is not a reply to the request outstanding. Today there is one, `log` (0xD0). Tools accept events at any time, also while waiting for a reply, and ignore types they do not know.

rules.name: resync
rules.text: Both sides decode byte by byte. On a wrong magic, a length above `max_payload` or a CRC mismatch the decoder drops one byte and searches again, so a frame after noise or a damaged frame is still found (the `streams` in the spec file are test cases). A frame cut short (a write that stopped part way, bytes lost on the way) is dropped once no byte has arrived for `idle_reset_ms`, so a request sent after that silence is found. Tools send each frame in one go (no pause of `idle_reset_ms` inside a frame).

rules.name: decoding
rules.text: Requests are decoded strictly: exactly the listed fields (the device checks lengths). Replies and events are decoded leniently: a tool ignores bytes after the fields it knows, so a later 1.x can add fields at the end. A reply or event marked `extensible: false` ends in `rest` or `text` and can never gain fields; a later version that needs more adds a command. An error reply holds the fields its `on_error` names, or the status alone. A common status sent as such (`state` before `hello`, `unsupported`, `busy`) always comes alone; a command that lists the same status among its own errors may send its `on_error` fields with it (`file.write_staged` and `boot.install` do for `state`), so decoders accept both.

rules.name: optional
rules.text: Optional fields come last and are all present or all absent (`optional_fields: all_or_none` on the layout): a `file.read` request is the path alone, or the path, offset and length.

rules.name: text
rules.text: Each `cstr` and `text` field states its encoding. `ascii`: bytes 0x01 to 0x7F. `utf-8`: file and folder names, which MTP clients and computers make with any characters. Limits: `max_bytes` counts bytes, not characters; a name never holds NUL, and `/` separates its parts; the device compares names as bytes, without Unicode normalisation (macOS may send decomposed accents, Windows composed ones, so one visible name can be two files). The device checks the `/yaffs2/` start, the parts (no empty, `.` or `..`), the NUL and control bytes (below 0x20, and 0x7F: `refused`), and passes every other byte to the stock file system unchanged: invalid UTF-8 is not refused.

rules.name: lengths
rules.text: The device checks request lengths exactly (except where a command says the payload is ignored); a request with the wrong length is refused with the status the command lists.

rules.name: versions
rules.text: Version 1 never renumbers a type or status, changes a meaning or changes a request layout. A later 1.x may add commands, status codes, events, `hello` keys and fields at the end of a reply: tools ignore reply bytes after the fields they know and `hello` keys they do not know, and show an unknown status by number as a failure. A tool stops when the major version in `proto` is not the one it speaks. Developer commands are outside this promise.

rules.name: destructive
rules.text: Commands marked destructive change what the OP-XY stores. Each binds its request to what it changes: the data it writes (a SHA-256 the tool sends again as confirmation; `library.set_default`: the id), or, for `file.delete`, `file.rmdir` and `file.mkdir`, the SHA-256 of the path bytes (without the NUL; `file.rename` and `file.copy`: both paths and the NUL between them). Tools must show the user what will be written or removed and ask before sending one.

statuses.name: ok
statuses.doc: done

statuses.name: bad_request
statuses.doc: malformed request: wrong length, a value out of its allowed set, an invalid path or id

statuses.name: unsupported
statuses.doc: this build does not answer this type (named `unknown` before 1.1)

statuses.name: state
statuses.doc: wrong order: no `hello` yet, nothing staged, staging incomplete; the same request will not succeed until something else changes

statuses.name: range
statuses.doc: an offset or address outside what the command allows

statuses.name: crc
statuses.doc: a CRC-32 differs (staged data, or a written file read back)

statuses.name: sha
statuses.doc: a SHA-256 differs (staged data or the confirmation token)

statuses.name: storage
statuses.doc: a file-system call on the device failed

statuses.name: not_found
statuses.doc: no such file

statuses.name: too_large
statuses.doc: a size above its limit (staging capacity, boot partition, whole-file read)

statuses.name: image
statuses.doc: the staged image is not acceptable for this install

statuses.name: install
statuses.doc: the boot-partition write or its read-back check failed

statuses.name: link
statuses.doc: processor A did not answer a request processor B passed on to it within its bound, or did not answer as XY Forever (B asks before it sends a change; 1.17: also before closing a write window left by an unanswered request); once the link is lost every command that needs A answers `link` at once and B stays at its menu until a power cycle

statuses.name: identity
statuses.doc: stock code in the device's memory differs from the checked bootloader image; the command did not run

statuses.name: refused
statuses.doc: well formed, but forbidden by the device's safety policy (a path the file engine refuses, or, for a change, outside the write area: since 1.13 all of `/yaffs2/` except `/yaffs2/bootloader.dev` and `/yaffs2/upgrade` with all below it; since 1.16 also a folder made, or a file written, copied or moved, more than 6 folders below `/yaffs2`, the stock dev-menu MTP's limit: docs/SAFETY.md)

statuses.name: busy
statuses.doc: a job (`mods.apply`) is running, or B is still closing A's write window after it ended (seconds); retry later, or `job.cancel` a running job

statuses.name: cancelled
statuses.doc: the job was cancelled (not sent by any command yet)

statuses.name: no_content
statuses.doc: the library entry's content is not installed in `/yaffs2/content/` (a mod set built on the device, or any entry while another one's content is installed): it is listed but does not boot as it is; make it the default to install its content. Added during 1.10 without a version bump: a build that reports 1.10 to 1.16 may answer another status for such an entry; every 1.17 build sends this one

statuses.name: started
statuses.doc: the request started a job (`library.set_default`: the content switch); follow it with `job.status`, whose end is the request's result

statuses.name: declined
statuses.doc: not allowed: the user answered Don't allow (Ask before USB control, `hello` `trust`); nothing was done (sent since 1.23)

statuses.name: waiting
statuses.doc: the device asks the user to allow this computer (no time limit); nothing done: show "Allow on your OP-XY", retry

statuses.name: serial_off
statuses.doc: serial is off: USB mode on the OP-XY is MTP (Settings, `hello` `serial`); nothing was done. Show "Serial is off on your OP-XY: Settings > USB mode"

common_errors.doc: the device has not answered a `hello` since it started; nothing was done
this build does not answer the type (it is not in `cmds`)

a job is running, or its write window is still closing after `job.status` said it ended: every command that needs processor A, the staging or a boot waits for it (`diag.status`, `screen.read`, `service.hold`, `job.status` and `job.cancel` are answered)
1.23: the device asks (`trust`); send it again
1.23: not allowed until unplugged or restarted
1.25: USB mode is MTP (`serial`); answered at once

commands.name: hello
commands.summary: greet the device; required before any other command

fields.name: info
fields.doc: ASCII, `XYF1` and then `key=value` items, separated by `;`; no NUL; at most `max_hello` bytes. The keys are listed below; tools ignore keys they do not know.

commands.doc: Answers in every state. While searching for the device, a tool may send `hello` every 0.5 s on the open port until a reply with status ok arrives. The reply tells the tool what the device supports: the protocol version, the release version and image it runs, the limits and the commands it answers. 1.1 added the keys from `mode` on (and `build`, replaced in 1.15 by `version` and `image`); a device without `cmds` is a pre-v1 device (see the rules).

commands.name: diag.status
commands.summary: device counters as tagged binary blocks

fields.name: blocks
fields.doc: a sequence of blocks `{u32 magic, u32 bytes, bytes...}`; the block layouts belong to the build (decoder: `xy_forever/census.py`) and change without notice

commands.doc: Development aid: the USB service's counters, the processor link, the file server, boot timing and the last dry-run boot.

commands.name: file.read
commands.summary: read a file, whole (at most 4096 bytes) or a range

fields.name: path
fields.doc: absolute path under `/yaffs2/`, NUL-terminated; no empty, `.` or `..` parts; no control bytes

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: first byte to read

fields.name: length
fields.doc: bytes to read, at most `max_read`

fields.name: data
fields.doc: ranged form: up to `length` bytes, fewer only at the end of the file; whole form: the whole file

commands.doc: Two forms: with `offset` and `length` (ranged), or the path alone (whole file, `too_large` above 4096 bytes). Use the ranged form: whole-file replies above 1 KiB hung the device in tests. To read any file, read ranges of `max_read` bytes from offset 0 until a reply holds fewer. An offset at or past the end of the file is ok with no data; `range` means the device's seek to the offset failed. A malformed path is `bad_request`; a well-formed one that the device's file policy refuses (a control byte) is `refused`.

commands.name: screen.read
commands.summary: read part of the display framebuffer (screenshot)

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: byte offset into the framebuffer

fields.name: framebuffer
fields.doc: the framebuffer's address (informational; also sent with `range`)

fields.name: pixels
fields.doc: up to `max_read` bytes from `offset`

commands.doc: Reads memory only. The framebuffer is 245760 (0x3C000) bytes: 480 columns, stored right to left, of 256 RGB565 pixels each, top to bottom; the visible picture is the first 216 pixels of each column. A screenshot reads offsets 0, 1024, 2048, ... until it has 245760 bytes. A request that is not exactly 4 bytes, an offset past the end or no valid framebuffer gives `range`.

commands.name: diag.peek
commands.summary: read device memory or registers (test only)

fields.name: address
fields.doc: first byte

fields.name: bytes
fields.doc: bytes to read

fields.name: address
fields.doc: the address read

fields.name: data
fields.doc: the bytes

commands.doc: Read-only, inside an allowlist of stock DDR, L2, L1 data and interrupt, reset and watchdog registers (usb_service.cpp peek_allowed, mmr_allowed); anything else is `range`.

commands.name: diag.engine_test
commands.summary: storage self-test from processor B's main loop (test only)

fields.name: hold_ms
fields.doc: how long to hold the storage window open in the middle

fields.name: step
fields.doc: last step reached (11 = all done)

fields.name: mounted
fields.doc: mount result

fields.name: space
fields.doc: storage info result

fields.name: stat
fields.doc: object info result

fields.name: dir
fields.doc: folder handle

fields.name: entries
fields.doc: folder entries listed

fields.name: closedir
fields.doc: folder close result

fields.name: fd
fields.doc: file handle

fields.name: read
fields.doc: bytes read

fields.name: closed
fields.doc: file close result

fields.name: wait_ms
fields.doc: time held

fields.name: stat2
fields.doc: object info result, again

fields.name: space2
fields.doc: storage info result, again

fields.name: unmounted
fields.doc: 1 when unmounted

fields.name: entry_bytes
fields.doc: unused (0)

fields.name: reserved
fields.doc: unused (0)

commands.doc: Runs the storage calls the old MTP code made, from B's main loop. The host waits 60 s plus hold_ms. To be renamed when the file engine (M2) replaces it.

commands.name: stage.begin
commands.summary: announce an image to stage in RAM

fields.name: size
fields.doc: image bytes, at most `max_stage`

fields.name: crc32
fields.doc: CRC-32 of the whole image

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: SHA-256 of the whole image

commands.doc: Starts a new staging and forgets any earlier one, also when it is refused (a `stage.data` after a refused `stage.begin` is `state`). Staging holds one image in processor B's RAM for `file.write_staged`, `boot.install` or `boot.uninstall`; it does not survive a restart. A size of 0 is also `too_large`.

commands.name: stage.data
commands.summary: send the next piece of the staged image

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: must equal the bytes received so far

fields.name: data
fields.doc: the next bytes; send `put_chunk` (1024) at a time

fields.name: received
fields.doc: bytes received so far

commands.doc: In order, without gaps: `range` when `offset` is not the bytes received so far or the data would pass the announced size; a resend of bytes already received, unchanged (a retry after a lost reply), is ok and `received` stays. `state` without a `stage.begin`, and also for a request without data.

commands.name: stage.end
commands.summary: check the staged image against its CRC-32 and SHA-256
commands.doc: `state` when not every announced byte arrived. After any error the staging is discarded; start again with `stage.begin`. A repeated `stage.end` after an ok one (a retry after a lost reply) is ok again and keeps the staging, until `boot.install`, `boot.uninstall` or `file.copy` uses it up or a `stage.begin` replaces it.

commands.name: file.write_staged
commands.summary: write the staged image to a file under /yaffs2/ (the write area)

fields.name: path
fields.doc: `/yaffs2/` and at least one more character, NUL-terminated; no empty, `.` or `..` parts; no control bytes; never `/yaffs2/bootloader.dev`, never inside `/yaffs2/upgrade/` (1.13); at most 6 folders below `/yaffs2` (1.16); missing folders are created

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: confirmation: the staged image's SHA-256 again

fields.name: written
fields.doc: bytes written

fields.name: readback_crc
fields.doc: CRC-32 of the file read back

commands.doc: Creates or replaces the file, reads it back and compares its CRC-32 (`crc` on a difference). A path the device's write check rejects is `refused` (1.0: `bad_request`): since 1.13 the write area is all of `/yaffs2/` except the dev-menu marker `/yaffs2/bootloader.dev` and the stock updater's inbox `/yaffs2/upgrade` (and anything inside it), both any ASCII case and also when reached through a link; also a path with an empty, `.` or `..` part, or a control byte. Before 1.13 the area was `/yaffs2/xy-forever/` and (1.7) `/yaffs2/content/`, no name holding `bootloader`; a request whose length does not match its path is `bad_request`. Needs a complete staging (`state` otherwise). The host tool restarts the device (`device.reboot`) and stages again before each write, the tested path; a second write in the same boot is untested. The host waits 60 s plus 1 s per 20000 bytes. To be replaced by streaming file commands.

commands.name: file.list
commands.summary: list one folder, a page at a time

fields.name: path
fields.doc: absolute folder path, `/yaffs2` or below, NUL-terminated; a trailing `/` is allowed

fields.name: skip
fields.doc: entries to pass over first: 0, then the previous `skip` plus `count` while `more` is 1

fields.name: count
fields.doc: entries in this page

fields.name: more

values.0: the folder ends in this page

fields.doc: whether the listing goes on

fields.name: entries
fields.doc: `count` entries, each `{u8 kind (0 file, 1 folder, 2 other), u32 size (bytes; 0 for a folder), u8 name_bytes, name}`: the name as UTF-8 bytes, 1 to 255 of them, without the folder or a NUL

commands.doc: One page of a folder's entries in the file system's order, without `.` and `..`; at most 1016 bytes of entries (a reply never passes `max_read`) and 64 entries per page. Each page opens the folder, passes over `skip` entries and closes it again, so a folder that changes between pages may show an entry twice or not at all; a page with `more` 1 may hold no entries. A path the device's file policy refuses (outside `/yaffs2`, an empty, `.` or `..` part, a control byte) is `refused`; a request whose length does not match its path is `bad_request`; a folder that does not exist (or a file) is `not_found`. Reads only: the write window stays as it is.

commands.name: file.delete
commands.summary: delete one file

fields.name: path
fields.doc: absolute path of a file in the write area (`file.write_staged`; 1.13: all of `/yaffs2/` but the marker and `upgrade/`), NUL-terminated

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: confirmation: the SHA-256 of the path bytes, without the NUL

fields.name: error
fields.doc: the device file system's error number (0 when none; 2 no such object, 21 a folder, 93 a folder not empty)

commands.doc: Removes the file through the device's write window (opened by the first change, closed by the device 8 s after the last one, as `file.write_staged`). Never `/yaffs2` itself, `/yaffs2/bootloader.dev` or `/yaffs2/upgrade` and anything inside it (any ASCII case, any spelling, also through a link; 1.13): `refused`, as every path the file policy refuses and every path outside `file.write_staged`'s write area; a wrong confirmation is `sha`. A missing file is `not_found`; a folder (error 21) or any other failure `storage`.

commands.name: file.rmdir
commands.summary: remove one empty folder

fields.name: path
fields.doc: absolute path of a folder in the write area (as `file.delete`), NUL-terminated

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: confirmation: the SHA-256 of the path bytes, without the NUL

fields.name: error
fields.doc: the device file system's error number (0 when none; 2 no such object, 20 not a folder, 93 not empty)

commands.doc: As `file.delete`, for an empty folder only: a folder that still holds entries is `state` (error 93; remove them first); a file (error 20) or any other failure is `storage`.

commands.name: file.mkdir
commands.summary: create one folder

fields.name: path
fields.doc: absolute path of the new folder in the write area (as `file.delete`), NUL-terminated; its parent must exist

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: confirmation: the SHA-256 of the path bytes, without the NUL

fields.name: error
fields.doc: the device file system's error number (0 when none; 2 the parent is missing, 17 the name exists)

commands.doc: Creates one folder through the write window (as `file.delete`). A missing parent is `not_found`; a name that exists already (error 17) or any other failure is `storage`. Paths the file policy refuses are `refused`, also (1.16) a folder more than 7 below `/yaffs2`.

commands.name: file.rename
commands.summary: rename or move one file or folder

fields.name: source
fields.doc: absolute path of a file or folder in the write area (as `file.delete`), NUL-terminated

fields.name: target
fields.doc: its new path, in the write area (never the marker, never in `upgrade/`); must not exist; its parent must; 1.16: a folder moved deeper is walked, and every folder in it must stay within 7 below `/yaffs2` (`refused`)

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: confirmation: the SHA-256 of the source bytes, a NUL and the target bytes

fields.name: error
fields.doc: the device file system's error number (0 when none; 2 no source or no target parent, 17 the target exists, 22 a folder into itself)

commands.doc: Renames, or moves between folders, a file or a whole folder through the write window (as `file.delete`). Both paths must pass `file.delete`'s checks (`refused`); a target that exists is `state` (nothing replaced); a missing source or target parent `not_found`; a folder into itself (error 22) or any other failure `storage`.

commands.name: file.copy
commands.summary: copy one file on the device

fields.name: source
fields.doc: absolute path of a file `file.read` may read, NUL-terminated

fields.name: target
fields.doc: the new file's path, as for `file.write_staged`; must not exist; its folder must

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: confirmation: the SHA-256 of the source bytes, a NUL and the target bytes

fields.name: bytes
fields.doc: bytes read from the source

fields.name: error
fields.doc: the device file system's error number (0 when none; 2 no target folder, 17 the target exists)

fields.name: partial
fields.doc: after a failed write: whether its target may remain (the device deletes it when it can)

commands.doc: Processor B reads the source whole into its staging buffer (at most `stage` bytes, else `too_large`) and writes it to the target as `file.write_staged` does, read back and compared (`crc`); the bytes never cross USB. A staging held before is discarded (`file.write_staged` and `boot.install` then answer `state`). A source `file.read` refuses, or a target `file.write_staged` refuses, is `refused`; a missing source or target folder `not_found`; a target that exists `state` (nothing replaced). After a failed write the device deletes the target. The host waits 60 s plus 1 s per 10000 bytes.

commands.name: file.write_begin
commands.summary: start a streamed, replace-safe write of one file

fields.name: path
fields.doc: the file to create or replace, as for `file.write_staged`; missing folders are created

fields.name: size
fields.doc: the file's size in bytes (0 allowed)

fields.name: crc
fields.doc: CRC-32 of the whole file

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: SHA-256 of the whole file: the confirmation `file.write_end` checks before the target changes

commands.doc: Opens the write window and creates `/yaffs2/xy-forever/tmp/put-<size>-<crc>` (8 lowercase hex digits each), replacing a leftover of that name; the target is not touched. Any earlier streamed write is abandoned first (its temporary file removed). A job in progress is `busy`. The bytes follow with `file.write_data`; `file.write_end` finishes. A write left without data for 5 s is abandoned the same way (a cut cable); temporary files left by a power cut are removed when the USB service next starts.

commands.name: file.write_data
commands.summary: send the next piece of a streamed write

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: must equal the bytes received so far

fields.name: data
fields.doc: the next bytes; send `put_chunk` (1024) at a time (one storage write each); processor B writes them before it answers

fields.name: received
fields.doc: bytes received and written so far

commands.doc: As `stage.data`, but each piece goes to the temporary file at once: `range` when `offset` is not the bytes received so far or the data would pass the announced size; a resend inside what was received is ok and `received` stays (its bytes are not compared: `file.write_end` checks the file). `state` without a streamed write in progress. A failed storage write (`storage`, `link`; a full storage is `storage`) abandons the write and removes the temporary file when it can.

commands.name: file.write_end
commands.summary: check the streamed file and rename it onto its target

fields.name: written
fields.doc: bytes written to the temporary file

fields.name: readback_crc
fields.doc: CRC-32 of the temporary file read back (0 when it was not read)

fields.name: error
fields.doc: the device file system's error number of the rename (0 when none; 21 the target is a folder)

commands.doc: Closes the temporary file, checks the received bytes' CRC-32 and SHA-256 against `file.write_begin` (`crc`, `sha`), reads the file back and compares its CRC-32 (`crc`), then processor A checks its size against its name and renames it onto the target in one step (yaffs replaces an existing file atomically: after a power cut the target is the old file or the new one, never a partial one). A target that is a folder is `storage` (error 21). On any failure the temporary file is removed and the target is unchanged. `state` when not every announced byte arrived or no streamed write is in progress. The host waits 60 s plus 1 s per 20000 bytes.

commands.name: boot.install
commands.summary: install the staged XY Forever build into the boot partition

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: confirmation: the staged image's SHA-256 again

fields.name: written
fields.doc: non-zero when the boot-partition writer finished

fields.name: partition
fields.doc: active boot partition read back (1 or 2; 0 = none)

fields.name: sectors
fields.doc: 512-byte sectors read back and compared

commands.doc: Accepts only a staged XY Forever build (its cold descriptor and a valid LDR structure; `image` otherwise) that fits the boot partition (`too_large`). Writes with the stock bootloader's own A/B boot-partition writer, then reads the partition back and compares every byte (`install` on any difference). Sends `log` events while it runs. A wrong-length request or no complete staging is `state`. Once the writer has run (`ok` or `install`) the staging is used up; a request refused before writing leaves it as it was. Takes minutes; the host waits up to 900 s.

commands.name: boot.uninstall
commands.summary: put the stock 1.2.1 os.ldr back into the boot partition

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: confirmation: the staged image's SHA-256 again

fields.name: written
fields.doc: non-zero when the boot-partition writer finished

fields.name: partition
fields.doc: active boot partition read back (1 or 2; 0 = none)

fields.name: sectors
fields.doc: 512-byte sectors read back and compared

commands.doc: As `boot.install`, but accepts only the exact stock OP-XY 1.2.1 `os.ldr` (2373336 bytes, SHA-256 `60358afdaa9b58ed40411602f6d5d4e1e3e02553ff2da7e25038e71dd002b52f`). From 1.26, both boot writers return to the ordinary file service after selecting user storage, allowing the host to restore the root OS file and clean up while XY Forever still runs. `boot.uninstall` itself leaves the files under `/yaffs2/xy-forever/` in place. The next restart boots stock 1.2.1.

commands.name: device.reboot
commands.summary: restart both processors

fields.name: target

values.0: the XY Forever menu with USB
values.2: the XY Forever menu with USB

fields.doc: where the device goes; without it: 2

commands.doc: The reply comes first; the device restarts about 50 ms later and the USB port goes away. Wait for the port to come back, then send `hello`. Targets 0 and 2 behave the same today. A target above 2 is `bad_request`; a payload that is neither empty nor 4 bytes counts as no target.

commands.name: menu.continue
commands.summary: leave the menu and boot the default firmware

fields.name: mode

values.1: dry run: the whole boot path without starting the OS, then back to the menu

fields.doc: without it: 0

commands.doc: After the ok reply the menu closes and USB goes away. Any other payload, or a mode above 1, is answered with `link` (not `bad_request`); so is a dry run processor A did not accept. Modes 2 and 3 ("open the menu with USB", outside boot model v3) are not part of v1: the menu is the home loop that answers this protocol, so a tool that is connected is already in the menu.

commands.name: service.hold
commands.summary: keep the device in the menu across restarts

fields.name: on
fields.doc: on: stay in the XY Forever menu (with USB) across `device.reboot` until power-off

commands.name: diag.key
commands.summary: inject a key event into the menu (test only)

fields.name: key
fields.doc: key number (xyf_host.py KEYS)

fields.name: pressed

commands.doc: As if the key changed on the OP-XY. A press can close the menu and end USB. Never answers the device's question "Allow this computer to control your OP-XY?", and never opens or picks the Ask before USB control setting (1.23).

commands.name: library.set_default
commands.summary: make a library entry the default firmware

fields.name: id
fields.doc: library entry id: 1-31 of `a-z 0-9 _ -`, NUL-terminated (the folder name under `/yaffs2/xy-forever/firmware/`)

fields.name: id_hash
fields.doc: CRC-32 of the id bytes, as sent to processor A (0 for `bad_request`)

commands.doc: An entry whose content is not installed (listed as content not installed) first gets its content: B starts the content switch as a job and answers `started` (`job.status`: phase `inputs`, `content` with done/total in files, `finish` while it writes the record and the default; `done` with detail = the id once the default is written; `failed` leaves the default unchanged, `error` 15 with code 1 when `/yaffs2/content/` is not the official set, 2 when the entry would replace an official file; a cut or failure leaves the content state switching, which nothing boots from until this request runs again). A build without the switch answers `no_content` (nothing sent to A). Processor A finds the one entry whose id has this hash and an `os.ldr`, and writes the next of the two state files (`/yaffs2/xy-forever/state-a.txt`, `state-b.txt`). ok means A finished and the menu shows the new default; `storage` means the menu's default did not change. Tools can confirm by reading both state files: the valid one with the higher `seq=` holds `default=ID`.

commands.name: library.boot
commands.summary: boot a library entry once, as PLAY on it in the library menu

fields.name: id
fields.doc: library entry id: 1-31 of `a-z 0-9 _ -`, NUL-terminated

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: confirmation: the SHA-256 of the id bytes, without the NUL

commands.doc: After the ok reply the menu closes, USB goes away and the entry boots once; the default and the state files do not change. Errors boot nothing: an entry the menu does not list is `not_found`, one it lists without an `os.ldr` (not selectable there) `state`, one whose content is not installed `no_content` (make it the default to install its content), a lost link `link`.

commands.summary: check that a firmware package on the device is official and that the device's own keys open it

fields.name: verdict

fields.name: reason

values.2: not a package, or its sizes differ from the file
values.3: an AES key index other than 0
values.4: the device's one-time-programmable memory gave no key

fields.name: public_key_sha256

commands.doc: Processor B reads the package header, verifies its P-224 signature with the public key in the device's one-time-programmable memory (OTP), then checks that the AES key there decrypts the package's name block and ZIP directory. It reads nothing else and changes nothing; the keys are read only for a well-formed header and nothing derived from them is sent. A cut (16-byte header: u32 `0x54434658`, package bytes, head bytes, tail offset; then the package's first head bytes and its bytes from the tail offset on) is checked as the package. ok: the check ran (see `verdict`); an error: the file could not be read.

Requires partition 0, closed write window, no open files, jobs, package lease or boot probe. After a link error or timeout send no further commands; a ROM hang needs a manual power cycle. No keys are exported.

Without a loaded stage 2 the type is not in `cmds` and gets `unsupported`; `hello` key `stage2` is then 0.

commands.name: mods.apply
commands.summary: start assembling mod firmware on the device (a job)

fields.doc: `mods/<generation>/`, the package set (as `profile`; 1.16: a flat store, `store.txt` `version=1` and each package's files under content names, docs/storage/mods.md; until 1.15 `mods/<profile>/<generation>/`, files 8 folders deep: #124)

fields.name: extensions
fields.doc: 0 to 8 extension ids, comma-separated (empty: none)

fields.name: name
fields.doc: the entry's `info.txt` name: 1-47 printable bytes, no space at either end

fields.name: flags

values.0: a known base only, standard memory
values.1: the user confirmed a base that is not a known one
values.2: the 4 MiB mod memory layout (since 1.12; the base's `expanded_module_base`)

fields.doc: bit 0: base trust; bit 1 (1.12): the 4 MiB layout, refused (`bad_request`) by a 1.11 device

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: confirmation: the SHA-256 of every request byte before it

fields.name: job
fields.doc: the job's id (0 when refused); its output folder is `/yaffs2/xy-forever/tmp/job-<id>/`

fields.name: missing

values.4: the generation's base package metadata (`manifest.json` or legacy `info.txt`)
values.5: the generation's `store.txt` (1.16; absent: an older layout, push the set again)

fields.doc: with `not_found`: the input the device lacks; with `unsupported` (1.16), 5: the generation's `store.txt` names a newer store version

commands.doc: Checks the request and that every input exists (`not_found`, `missing` says which), makes the output folder and answers at once; processor B then runs the job in small steps from its menu loop, which stays live (`job.status`, `job.cancel`). Reads only the generation's packages, the base entry, the stock catalog and the output; writes only the output folder: an entry's files as `<name>.part`, read back, renamed, `os.ldr` last. A failed or cancelled job leaves no `os.ldr`; it removes its files and folders (`debris` 1 in `job.status` when it could not). Before the job's first step B removes leftover `tmp/job-*` folders (bounded); since 1.17 also when its USB service starts. A finished entry becomes library entry `mods-a` or `mods-b` (phase `finish`, detail `commit`): never the default or the boot-once entry; the absent one, else the one not written last; the old entry is renamed into `tmp/` first, then the new one into `firmware/`, then the old one removed. It is listed with its content not installed (`no_content`). A staged upload in progress is `busy`; no free job id, or both mods ids are the default and the boot-once entry, `state`.

fields.name: phase

fields.name: total
fields.doc: of total (0: not known ahead)

fields.name: error
fields.doc: why it failed (`native/mod_job.hpp`; 12 with code 18: a base that is not a known one, not confirmed; 17: also the library commit; 21: processor A did not answer)

fields.name: elapsed_ms
fields.doc: since the start (to the end once final)

fields.name: steps

fields.name: longest_ms
fields.doc: the longest menu-loop pass the job took

fields.name: peak
fields.doc: work-region bytes used at most

fields.name: debris

values.1: a failed job's files or folders may remain in its output folder

fields.doc: after a failed or cancelled job

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: ASCII, NUL-padded: which file, object, edit or check; when done, the library entry id (also for a content switch)

commands.doc: A job id this boot has not started (none yet, for 0) is `not_found`.

commands.name: job.cancel
commands.summary: stop the running job

fields.name: job
fields.doc: the job's id; 0: the running job

fields.name: debris

values.1: files or folders may remain in its output folder

fields.doc: after the clean-up

commands.doc: Removes what the job wrote and answers once that is done; a job that already ended, or is in its library commit (phase `finish`, detail `commit`), or a content switch (`library.set_default`), is `state`.

commands.name: package.session
commands.summary: exclude other storage jobs during a host package transaction

fields.name: version
fields.doc: session ABI version; a newer version is unsupported

fields.name: action
fields.doc: 0 acquire, 1 renew, 2 release

fields.name: token
fields.doc: host-chosen token; renew and release must match the acquired token

commands.doc: Host package transactions stage and verify packages through existing file RPCs, then publish by one directory rename. An acquired session excludes MTP, other jobs, boots and the idle scratch sweep, but permits file.read/list/delete/rmdir/mkdir/rename and streamed writes. Renew before each operation. After ten seconds without requests and with no upload, the session is abandoned and idle scratch cleanup resumes. Release closes the write window asynchronously; retry subsequent file requests while busy. This is cooperative exclusion for one CDC client, not an authorization boundary. Raw file/MTP operations remain available outside a package transaction.

commands.name: package.list
commands.summary: list packages and their exact identity

fields.name: version
fields.doc: API version: 1; newer is unsupported

fields.name: area
fields.doc: 0 inbox, 1 firmware library, 2 mods

fields.name: outer
fields.doc: cursor, initially 0

fields.name: inner
fields.doc: mod-package cursor within generation; otherwise 0

fields.name: version
fields.doc: reply format: 1

fields.name: outer
fields.doc: next cursor

fields.name: inner
fields.doc: next inner cursor

fields.name: more
fields.doc: 1: request next page, 0: end

fields.name: item
fields.doc: At most one item: LF key=value ASCII text; empty on end

commands.doc: One item per page, in filesystem order. Start both cursors at zero and use the returned cursors until more is zero. Area 2 walks mods/<generation>/<package>. Item keys: id (relative to area), type, version, sha256 (manifest image hash, or single-file hash), identity (SHA-256 of exact files.sha256 bytes; absent list: the single file itself), needs_os, generation, profile, valid (strict manifest admitted; 0 for legacy or unknown). Inbox files are recognised by bytes, never extension. Unknown or incomplete folders remain visible with valid=0 and an empty identity when no list or single image exists. The caller waits up to 600 seconds (large official inbox files are streamed, never buffered whole). Hashing is streamed in menu-loop slices while other storage commands return busy. Directory contents may change between pages; use package.session for a stable cooperative snapshot. This read never changes admission or legacy boot semantics.

commands.name: state.get
commands.summary: read boot slots, content record and durable job intent

fields.name: version
fields.doc: API version: 1; newer is unsupported

fields.name: part
fields.doc: 0 state-a, 1 state-b, 2 legacy state, 3 content-state, 4 journal

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: requested offset

fields.name: text
fields.doc: Exact stored bytes (up to 1004); slot CRCs and journal version remain visible

commands.doc: Pages the existing records without rewriting or interpreting unknown fields. The journal falls back to job.old when job.txt is absent; content falls back to content-state.old. A missing part is not_found. The valid highest-sequence boot slot wins, with the existing legacy fallback. Journal version 1 names target, previous entry, source identities, default intent and undo direction; a newer or malformed journal stays on disk and the menu explains the refusal. Missing source: the menu offers Set default to the previous entry, also available through library.set_default; no separate repair command.

fields.name: version

fields.doc: low 32 bits of free bytes

fields.name: free_high

A successful statfs return accepts a stale YAFFS errno; a zero block size is storage failure, and zero free blocks is valid. Does not mount storage for writing.

commands.name: dev.a_rehearsal
commands.summary: transfer staged B input to A and admit it without writing

fields.name: version
fields.doc: format 1; newer is unsupported

fields.name: operation
fields.doc: 0 start, 1 status, 2 cancel

fields.name: kind

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: start only: staged input token

fields.name: version
fields.doc: reply format 1

fields.name: phase
fields.doc: 0 finished or idle, 1..8 cooperative transfer phase

fields.name: done
fields.doc: A-acknowledged bytes

fields.name: total
fields.doc: input bytes

fields.name: crc32

commands.doc: Developer RAM-only rehearsal. Starts from the current stage.end-verified B input. Transfers contiguous chunks into A-owned staging, checks chunk and full CRC/SHA on A, and applies the existing boot.install or boot.uninstall policy independently on A. Poll status until phase 0; result 0 plus A SHA-256 proves admission. Cancel and deadline abort the transfer. Success collects A proof then releases A ownership. No boot-partition write, filesystem write, read-write mount or reset. A delayed request never blocks USB/status. A link failure stops without reset, retry or fallback; ordinary lost-link behavior is retained. Shipping boot.install and boot.uninstall are unchanged.

These are the inputs a plain power-on converges to (builds, installs content, sets the default) before it boots: docs/storage/state.md.

Operation 6: the last import's timing on B, u32 each: the bucket count n, n sums in units of 1024 cycles of the 400 MHz clock, then the source reads, pieces put, members written and member bytes (`PackClock`, target/usb_service_pack_import.ipp; 1.29 dropped the first bucket, A's hash). commands.doc: Import decrypts the .tfw with the device's key, checks every member's CRC-32 and SHA-256 (not the .tfw signature, since 1.29) and publishes one complete kept pack. Poll status until completion. Cancel while opening or staging leaves the current packs intact. Enable moves a retained pack into the live packs (not tested on this firmware).

events.name: log

fields.name: ms

fields.name: text
fields.doc: ASCII, no NUL, at most `max_log_text` bytes

events.doc: Sent with seq 0 while an install writes the boot partition, as long as the tool keeps reading (the device stops sending after the first line that cannot be delivered). Lines like `xyf install step N value 0x...` mark the install's steps.

hello.doc: The `hello` text: `XYF1`, then these keys in this order, each as `;key=value`. A build's text never changes while it runs, except `stage2` and the stage-2 command's bit of `cmds`: both are set before the reply to the first `hello` of a boot when stage 2 loads, and cleared again if stage 2 stops answering as it should; and (1.23) `confirm`, once the device has read its settings and when Ask before USB control is saved, and `trust`, as the question is asked and answered; and (1.25) `serial`, as USB mode is picked. Tools ignore keys they do not know and must not rely on the order.

keys.name: install
keys.doc: the boot-partition writer `boot.install` uses (the stock bootloader's own, at 0x88a06a7e)

keys.name: version
keys.doc: XY Forever release version `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (`0.1.0` the first); builds between two releases carry the same one

keys.name: image
keys.doc: the os.ldr this boot runs: the first 8 lowercase hex digits of its SHA-256, which name its build (`builds/<image>/`). The device hashes the image the stock bootloader read from the boot partition, however it was installed (`boot.install` or the dev menu), once per boot, before its first `hello` reply; `unknown` when no XY Forever image is there to hash

keys.name: mode
keys.doc: build mode (`product`, the only mode with this service)

keys.name: cmds
keys.doc: the request types this build answers: 32 lowercase hex digits, a 128-bit number written most significant digit first, in which bit t (value 2^t) is set when type t is answered (Python: `int(cmds, 16) >> t & 1`). Derived from each command's build switch when the build is compiled; the stage-2 command's bit is set at run time while stage 2 is loaded

keys.name: dev
keys.doc: `1` when the build answers developer commands; absent otherwise

keys.name: confirm
keys.doc: Ask before USB control (Settings): `1` when the first command but `hello` of a connection makes the device ask "Allow this computer to control your OP-XY?" (`trust`), `0` when every command runs at once. No USB command changes it, only the device's Settings row with its own keys; file transfers (MTP, the serial file commands) stay open and can replace or delete `settings.txt` like any file; `1` until the device has read its settings (the default when it has none)

keys.name: trust
keys.doc: the question's state on this connection: `none` (not asked: the setting is off, or no command but `hello` came yet), `asking` (every command but `hello` answers `waiting`), `allowed` (the user allowed: commands run), `refused` (the user did not: every command but `hello` answers `declined`). An answer lasts until the USB cable is unplugged (seen as a USB bus reset; closing and reopening the port keeps it) or the device restarts; on the stock serial fallback (no composite) the device sees no unplug, so until it restarts

keys.name: serial
keys.doc: USB mode (Settings) for serial: `on`, or `off` when it is MTP: then every command but `hello` answers `serial_off` and tools show "Serial is off on your OP-XY: Settings > USB mode". The USB device always carries both MTP and serial; the mode switches each in place (with Serial, MTP sessions are refused), the moment it is picked, never re-enumerating

keys.name: stage2
keys.doc: the loaded stage 2's version, decimal; `0` when none is loaded (no file, or it failed a check). Always the last key

golden.name: hello, answered by a pre-v1 device
any request before hello is refused
a write path outside the write area is refused
a common status comes alone, whatever on_error says

streams.name: noise before a frame
streams.doc: bytes that are not a frame, including a lone `X` and an `X` not followed by `F`, then `hello`

streams.name: a bad CRC, then a good frame
streams.doc: `hello` seq 2 with its last CRC byte changed is dropped; `hello` seq 3 after it is found

streams.name: a frame split at every byte
streams.doc: `hello` seq 4 arriving one byte per read

streams.name: two frames back to back
streams.doc: `hello` seq 5 and `stage.end` seq 6 in one read: both are found, in order

streams.name: an oversized length
streams.doc: a header announcing 4161 bytes (one above `max_payload`) is noise; `hello` seq 8 after it is found

streams.name: a frame cut short, then a frame
streams.doc: the first 10 of the 16 bytes of `screen.read` seq 9, then `hello` seq 10: the parser takes `hello`'s first 6 bytes as the rest of the cut frame, the CRC fails, and the rescan finds `hello`

streams.name: frames split across reads
streams.doc: `hello` seq 11 and `stage.end` seq 12 cut into reads of 5, 10 and 9 bytes, the second spanning both frames

streams.name: an event and a reply back to back
streams.doc: a `log` event and the `boot.install` reply seq 13 in one read

streams.name: noise and a reply split across reads
streams.doc: `XF` and a byte, then the `stage.data` reply seq 14 in three reads

reserved.doc: Numbers reserved for later items, and retired numbers that are never used again. Not answered by any build: nothing here exists on the wire.

types.doc: retired, never reused: the test command `diag.guard` until 1.13 (the watchdog guard was removed in 1.14)
retired, never reused: the test command `diag.hang` until 1.13
events, seq 0 (0xD0 is log today; progress 0xD1 with #14)
